comments.note: The null-guard in the resolveStore() ternary (typeof ... === 'object' && ... !== null) is correct defensive TypeScript — typeof null === 'object' in JS, so the check is necessary. Well-executed.

Gold Nugget: The string | { store: LedgerStore } overload pattern used in propagateDependencyUnblock and propagateDependencyReblock is a reusable architectural idiom — it allows top-level callers to provide a project path while internal callers can pass a pre-opened store, avoiding redundant LedgerStore construction and potential double-locking. This pattern is worth capturing in tech-stack.md or constraints.md for future developers who write functions with similar dual-caller requirements.
